Summarize an admiral_df Dataset

Source: R/admiral_df.R
summary.admiral_df.Rd

Reports what a dataset contains and whether it has one record per key variable combination. This is useful after a derivation, e.g. to check that derive_param_computed() added the records that were expected.

The summary always shows the dataset name and ADaM class, the number of subjects, observations and variables, and the record structure. It then adds the information for the dataset class (see get_dataset_class()):

  • ADSL: subjects per treatment arm, the population flag counts, the subject flow (randomized, treated, completed), the treatment duration, the end of study status, the deaths and their causes, and the age and sex of the subjects.

  • BDS/MDBDS: records, subjects, and visits per parameter, with the distribution of AVAL for numeric parameters and the distinct AVALC values for character ones, the analysis visits, the derived records per DTYPE, and checks for parameters with neither AVAL nor AVALC populated and for more than one baseline record (ABLFL) per subject, parameter, and BASETYPE.

  • OCCDS/MDOCCDS: the number of distinct terms, the treatment-emergent, and the serious vs total records, the records per severity and per toxicity grade, and a check for more than one "Y" per group in the occurrence flags (AOCCFL, AOCCSFL, AOCCPFL, ...).

  • TTE/MDTTE: events and censored per parameter.

If adsl is supplied, the summary also compares the dataset with it, see the adsl argument.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'admiral_df'
summary(object, adsl = NULL, max_params = 10, ...)

Arguments

object

An admiral_df object

Default value

none

adsl

The subject-level dataset to compare object with

If it is supplied, the summary also reports how many of the ADSL subjects have records, overall, within the safety population (SAFFL), and per treatment arm; checks that every subject of object is in ADSL; and, for an OCCDS dataset, reports the subjects with a treatment-emergent record (TRTEMFL) out of the safety population, or out of ADSL if there is no SAFFL.

Subjects are matched by the variables they are counted by (see Details), which must be in adsl, and adsl must have one record per subject. adsl is ignored, with a warning, for a dataset of class "ADSL" and for a dataset without any of these variables.

Permitted values

a data frame or NULL

Default value

NULL

max_params

The maximum number of parameters printed per table

A BDS or TTE dataset with more parameters than this prints the first max_params of them, and the number left out. All of them are in the returned object.

Permitted values

a positive integer

Default value

10

...

Not used

Default value

none

Value

An object of class summary_admiral_df, a named list which is printed by print.summary_admiral_df().

Details

The checks (e.g. of the record structure) report problems in the summary only: they never raise an error or a warning, so summary() can be called anywhere in a derivation pipeline. Each item is only reported when the variables it needs are in the dataset, so a dataset which is still being derived gives a shorter summary rather than an error.

The record structure is checked against the keys stored by admiral_df(). Keys are never inferred, so if none were stored the structure is not checked.

Subjects are counted by USUBJID if it is present, as the other subject keys (e.g. STUDYID) may not be populated on records added by a derivation. Otherwise the subject keys (get_admiral_option("subject_keys")) are used if all of them are in the dataset, as only together do they identify a subject. A record with any of these NA belongs to no subject, so it is not counted as one.

The records of a medical device dataset (ADDL, MDBDS, MDTTE, MDOCCDS) belong to a device rather than a subject, so devices are counted by SPDEVID, and the per-parameter counts and the checks are per device. USUBJID is optional in these datasets; if it is present the subjects are counted as well, and it is what adsl is matched by.

The dataset name is the one stored by admiral_df() or, failing that, the name of the variable summary() was called on.

See also

The admiral_df Class: admiral_df(), get_dataset_class(), get_dataset_keys(), get_dataset_name()

Examples

Summarizing a BDS dataset after a derivation

library(tibble)
library(dplyr, warn.conflicts = FALSE)

advs <- tribble(
  ~USUBJID,      ~PARAMCD, ~AVAL, ~AVISIT,
  "01-701-1015", "DIABP",     51, "BASELINE",
  "01-701-1015", "SYSBP",    121, "BASELINE",
  "01-701-1028", "DIABP",     79, "BASELINE",
  "01-701-1028", "SYSBP",    130, "BASELINE"
) %>%
  mutate(STUDYID = "PILOT01")

advs <- derive_param_computed(
  advs,
  by_vars = exprs(STUDYID, USUBJID, AVISIT),
  parameters = c("SYSBP", "DIABP"),
  set_values_to = exprs(
    AVAL = (AVAL.SYSBP + 2 * AVAL.DIABP) / 3,
    PARAMCD = "MAP"
  )
)

summary(advs)
#> ── advs: BDS summary ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> Subjects (USUBJID): 2
#> Observations: 6 | Variables: 5
#> i Structure: not checked, no keys set (see `admiral_df()`)
#> 3 numeric parameters (AVAL):
#>   PARAMCD  records  subjects  visits  missing    min  median  max
#>   DIABP          2         2       1        0     51      65   79
#>   MAP            2         2       1        0  74.33   85.17   96
#>   SYSBP          2         2       1        0    121   125.5  130
#> Analysis visits (AVISIT): BASELINE
#> ✔ Checks passed: every parameter has AVAL or AVALC populated

Checking against declared keys

The record structure is only checked once the keys have been stored with admiral_df().

advs <- admiral_df(
  advs,
  dataset_keys = exprs(USUBJID, PARAMCD, AVISIT),
  dataset_name = "ADVS"
)

summary(advs)
#> ── ADVS: BDS summary ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> Subjects (USUBJID): 2
#> Observations: 6 | Variables: 5
#> ✔ Structure: one record per USUBJID, PARAMCD, AVISIT
#> 3 numeric parameters (AVAL):
#>   PARAMCD  records  subjects  visits  missing    min  median  max
#>   DIABP          2         2       1        0     51      65   79
#>   MAP            2         2       1        0  74.33   85.17   96
#>   SYSBP          2         2       1        0    121   125.5  130
#> Analysis visits (AVISIT): BASELINE
#> ✔ Checks passed: every parameter has AVAL or AVALC populated

Comparing with ADSL

Supplying the ADSL shows the subjects without records, and checks that every subject of the dataset is in the ADSL.

adsl <- tribble(
  ~STUDYID,  ~USUBJID,      ~SAFFL, ~TRT01A,
  "PILOT01", "01-701-1015", "Y",    "Placebo",
  "PILOT01", "01-701-1028", "Y",    "Xanomeline High Dose",
  "PILOT01", "01-701-1034", "N",    NA
)

summary(advs, adsl = adsl)
#> ── ADVS: BDS summary ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> Subjects (USUBJID): 2
#> Observations: 6 | Variables: 5
#> ✔ Structure: one record per USUBJID, PARAMCD, AVISIT
#> 3 numeric parameters (AVAL):
#>   PARAMCD  records  subjects  visits  missing    min  median  max
#>   DIABP          2         2       1        0     51      65   79
#>   MAP            2         2       1        0  74.33   85.17   96
#>   SYSBP          2         2       1        0    121   125.5  130
#> Analysis visits (AVISIT): BASELINE
#> ✔ Checks passed: every parameter has AVAL or AVALC populated
#> Subjects with records out of ADSL: 2 of 3 (66.7%) | safety population 2 of 2
#> (100.0%)
#> Subjects with records per arm (TRT01A): Placebo: 1 of 1 | Xanomeline High Dose:
#> 1 of 1 | NA: 0 of 1
#> ✔ Checks passed: all subjects with records are in ADSL
